segs.text: Hello, and welcome! If you are a candidate for the ASCON Public Service Examination, this video is for you.
I'll walk you through everything you need to know: before, during, and after your exam. And stay sharp, because there's a quick quiz along the way!
Step one. Open the browser on your device, and visit the official ASCON website: ascon.gov.ng.
On the homepage, look for the link to the CBT examination portal.
Click it, and the examination sign-in page opens. That's your gateway.
Now, what should you bring on exam day?
Your username and password, exactly as issued to you.
A valid means of identification.
Your device: a laptop, tablet, or smartphone. Fully charged, with a charger or power bank.
Enough internet data for a stable connection.
And for the theory paper, bring pens and plain sheets of paper.
Pro tip: arrive early, so you are settled and connected before the countdown begins.
Here's good news. You are allowed to bring your own laptop, smartphone, or tablet, and use it to write the examination.
But there is one condition you cannot skip. Your device location must be switched on, at the examination venue.
When the portal asks for your location, tap Allow. Until your location is confirmed, the continue button stays locked. No location, no exam!
Let's walk through signing in. First, enter your username, and tap Continue.
Next, type your password, and sign in.
Read the instructions carefully. Make sure your location is on, tick the box to accept the terms, and continue.
Confirm your details: your name, present post, promotion post, and grade level. If anything is wrong, correct it right there.
Then you'll see your paper: the areas you'll be examined on, the number of questions, and the duration. When the countdown reaches zero, tap Start Examination.
Inside the exam, the timer sits at the top. Pick your answer, then move with Next and Previous.
The question palette lets you jump to any question, and shows what you've answered at a glance.
Every answer is saved instantly, and backed up to the server automatically.
When five minutes remain, the timer turns red. When time runs out, your paper is submitted automatically. If you finish early, tap Submit Paper.
Now, listen closely. This part matters most.
While you write, the system is monitoring in the background.
Switching browser tabs or pages. Minimizing the exam window. Opening another app, like WhatsApp or a search engine.
Listening to audio or using earpieces in the background. Copying and pasting content.
Every one of these is detected. A warning appears, and each incident is counted, and recorded against you as examination malpractice.
So, stay on the exam window, from the first question to the last.
Quick check! Allowed, or malpractice? Think fast.
Number one. Writing the exam on your own smartphone, with location switched on.
Allowed! That's exactly right.
Number two. Quickly switching to WhatsApp to read a message.
Malpractice! Leaving the exam window is recorded.
Number three. Opening a new tab to search for an answer.
Malpractice! Stay on the exam page.
Number four. Wearing earpieces, and listening to audio during the exam.
Malpractice again! Keep your ears free, and your focus on the screen.
After Part A, you move on to the Theory, Part B, which has its own timer.
Download or print the answer sheet if it's provided, and write your answers clearly on paper.
Then take a clear photo of each page, and upload it. You can upload several pages. Just make sure everything is uploaded before the time runs out.
And remember: leaving the window during Part B is recorded too.
And when you're done?
Wait for the Examination Complete screen. That's your confirmation that your submission has been recorded.
Where enabled, your Part A score is shown immediately. Your theory answers are marked separately, and the overall result is released by the examination office.
Each candidate can take the examination only once. After you submit, you cannot sit it again.
Let's recap the golden rules.
Come prepared. Location on. Stay on the exam window. Upload before time. Wait for confirmation.
Do these, and you're all set. Best of luck in your examination!
